Regulations on the Training of Judges

Fa Fa [2000] No. 24

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China for the purpose of continuously improving the political and professional qualities of judges and meeting the needs of the development of trial work.

Article 2 Training of judges shall be divided into qualification training for appointment, promotion, and continuation in office, as well as other training.

Persons to be appointed as judges and persons to be appointed as presidents and vice-presidents of people's courts shall receive qualification training for appointment.

Promotion to senior judge shall be subject to qualification training for promotion.

Judges shall regularly receive qualification training for continuation in office.

Article 3 Judges have the right and obligation to receive training in accordance with the law.

Article 4 Training of judges shall be implemented under unified leadership, unified planning, centralized responsibility, and分级 implementation.

Article 5 Training of judges shall adhere to the principles of integrating theory with practice, combining study with application, teaching according to needs, and emphasizing practical results.

Article 6 Persons to be appointed as judges and incumbent judges may assume office, be promoted, or continue to perform their duties only after receiving the prescribed training and passing the examination.

Chapter II Organization and Administration

Article 7 Training of judges shall be implemented under a two-level administrative system. The Supreme People's Court shall uniformly lead the training of judges in courts nationwide, and the High People's Courts shall lead the training of judges in the people's courts within their respective jurisdictions.

Article 8 The education and training administrative departments of the Supreme People's Court and High People's Courts shall be responsible for the planning, administration, and coordination of judge training.

Article 9 The Supreme People's Court shall establish the National Judges College.

High People's Courts shall establish judge training institutions such as provincial judges colleges, judges advanced study institutes, and judges training institutes.

With the approval of the High People's Court, judge training institutions at the prefecture (city) level may be established as needed and conditions permit.

Judge training institutions at all levels shall be responsible for organizing and implementing various judge training programs.

Article 10 The National Judges College undertakes:
(1) Qualification training for appointment of presidents and vice-presidents of High and Intermediate People's Courts;
(2) Qualification training for promotion to senior judge;
(3) Qualification training for continuation in office of judges of the Supreme People's Court;
(4) Qualification training for continuation in office of senior judges of local people's courts at all levels;
(5) Training of teaching staff for local judge training institutions;
(6) Other training designated by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 11 Provincial judges colleges or other judge training institutions undertake:
(1) Qualification training for appointment of presidents and vice-presidents of Basic People's Courts;
(2) Qualification training for persons to be appointed as judges of local people's courts at all levels;
(3) Qualification training for continuation in office of judges below the rank of Grade One in local people's courts at all levels;
(4) Other training designated by the High People's Court;
(5) Training entrusted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 12 Judge training institutions at the prefecture (city) level undertake training tasks authorized by the High People's Court.

Article 13 The Supreme People's Court shall establish a Judges Training Textbook Compilation and Review Committee to uniformly plan and organize the compilation and review of teaching syllabi and textbooks for various types of judge training.

With the approval of the Judges Training Textbook Compilation and Review Committee, High People's Courts may compile supplementary teaching materials for judge training as needed.

Chapter III Content and Forms

Article 14 Judge training shall focus on the education of judges' professional ethics and professional competence, improving judges' ability to apply the law in hearing cases and to draft judicial documents. The specific content of judge training shall be tailored according to the needs of different training targets.

Article 15 Qualification training for appointment of presidents and vice-presidents of people's courts shall, in accordance with post requirements, focus on training to improve the management and professional capabilities necessary for performing post duties. The training period shall not be less than three months.

Qualification training for appointment of judges shall focus on professional ethics education, relevant legal theory, basic post theory, and trial practice. The training period shall not be less than three months.

Qualification training for continuation in office shall focus on updating professional knowledge for the post and improving trial skills. Judges shall receive qualification training for continuation in office once every three years. The training period shall not be less than one month.

Qualification training for promotion to senior judge shall focus on the knowledge and skills necessary for senior judges to perform their post duties. The training period shall not be less than two months.

Other training mainly refers to training on new laws and regulations, trial practice research, etc. The training period may be determined according to actual circumstances.

Article 16 Judge training shall mainly be conducted through centralized training while off duty. It may also be conducted in segments with accumulated class hours.

Article 17 Judge training shall strengthen international exchanges and cooperation. Judges may be selected to study abroad in accordance with relevant state regulations, or foreign legal experts, professors, and judges may be invited to give special lectures in China.

Chapter IV Conditions and Guarantees

Article 18 The teaching staff for judge training shall be a combination of full-time and part-time teachers, with part-time teachers as the main component.

Article 19 Judge training institutions shall establish a team of full-time teachers and administrative staff commensurate with the training tasks.

Full-time teachers engaged in judge training shall have a bachelor's degree or higher, high political and professional qualities, and the corresponding judge qualifications and trial work experience. Full-time teachers for judge training shall generally be selected from among judges.

Full-time teachers of judge training institutions shall participate in trial work in a planned manner to enrich practical experience, thereby enhancing the pertinence of training and teaching.

Article 20 In the budget, a separate line item shall be set aside for education and training funds for judges of people's courts at all levels.

Education and training funds for judges must be used for designated purposes only and shall not be intercepted, misappropriated, or diverted.

Education and training funds for judges shall be increased year by year along with the growth of the national economy and the needs of judge training.

Article 21 Judge training institutions shall have training bases, library materials, teaching equipment, and other training conditions commensurate with the training tasks.

Article 22 Judge training institutions at all levels may reasonably charge training fees in accordance with relevant state regulations.

Chapter V Assessment and Responsibility

Article 23 The judge management departments of people's courts shall, in accordance with the scope of authority, establish training archives for judges under their jurisdiction. The training record, results, and evaluations of judges participating in training shall be placed in their personal files.

Article 24 The people's court that has established a judge training institution shall establish and improve the assessment system for judge training, and strictly enforce the verification and issuance system for the Certificate of Qualification for various types of judge qualification training.

The Certificate of Qualification for judge qualification training shall be uniformly printed by the Supreme People's Court.

The Certificate of Qualification for various types of qualification training held by the National Judges College shall be verified and issued by the education and training administrative department of the Supreme People's Court and the National Judges College.

The Certificate of Qualification for various types of qualification training held by provincial judge training institutions shall be verified and issued by the education and training administrative department of the High People's Court and the provincial judge training institution.

Certificates of Completion for other training shall be printed and issued by judge training institutions at all levels.

Article 25 People's courts at all levels shall guarantee the right of judges to receive training in accordance with the law.

Judges participating in training shall enjoy the salary and welfare benefits of incumbent judges during the training period, and training fees, travel expenses, etc., shall be reimbursed in accordance with regulations.

Article 26 If a judge, without justifiable reasons, refuses to participate in training, the people's court where he or she works shall urge him or her to correct the behavior and may, depending on the circumstances, give criticism and education or even disqualify him or her from continuation in office or promotion.

Article 27 The Supreme People's Court and High People's Courts that have established judge training institutions at the prefecture (city) level shall establish a judge training evaluation system, and regularly inspect and evaluate the training conditions and training quality of judge training institutions. Judge training institutions that fail to meet the requirements upon evaluation shall rectify within a prescribed time limit. If they fail to rectify within the time limit, they shall be ordered to cease judge training work.

Chapter VI Supplementary Provisions

Article 28 The training of other staff of people's courts shall be implemented by reference to these Regulations.

Article 29 The training of judges in specialized courts shall be implemented by the specialized courts formulating specific measures by reference to these Regulations, which shall be implemented after approval by the competent authority. It may also be carried out relying on the National Judges College and provincial judge training institutions.

Article 30 High People's Courts may formulate implementation measures based on local actual conditions.

Article 31 These Regulations shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 32 These Regulations shall come into effect as of January 1, 2001.

October 20, 2000
